subject: life-orientation-sp
description: Life Orientation Senior Phase (Grades 7–9) question bank. One 20-item pool per atomic skill (the topic key IS the skill id). Content subject: 0.6 pass mark, mastery via lib/content-mastery.ts. Tap-only; no free text. Physical Education excluded.

LO.G7.DS.A1.title: Self-image
LO.G7.DS.A1.description: Development of the self in society (CAPS G7 T1) — Development of the self in society: Self-image.
LO.G7.DS.A1.strand: Development of the self in society · Term 1
LO.G7.DS.A1.caps_topic: Development of the self in society
LO.G7.DS.A1.recovery_strategy: Your self-image is how you see yourself; positive actions and respect build it up.

questions.question: What does the term 'self-image' mean?
options: The way you see and feel about yourself
questions.expected: The way you see and feel about yourself
questions.memo: Self-image is the picture you hold of yourself — your view of your own worth, looks and abilities.

questions.question: A positive self-image means thinking you are perfect and never make mistakes.
questions.memo: A healthy self-image is realistic — you value yourself while accepting that everyone has flaws and can grow.

questions.question: Thabo keeps telling himself 'I am hopeless at everything.' What is the BEST way for him to build a healthier self-image?
options: Notice his real strengths and speak kindly to himself
Compare himself to others all day
Wait for others to praise him first
questions.expected: Notice his real strengths and speak kindly to himself
questions.memo: Recognising your genuine strengths and using positive self-talk builds a healthier self-image.

questions.question: Treating yourself with kindness and valuing your own worth is called respect for ____.
questions.memo: Respect for self means valuing who you are; it is the foundation of a healthy self-image.

questions.question: Which action shows RESPECT for others' self-image?
options: Encouraging a classmate who is nervous
questions.expected: Encouraging a classmate who is nervous
questions.memo: Encouraging and including others lifts their self-image; mocking or excluding harms it.

questions.question: Respecting diversity means valuing people who are different from you.
questions.memo: Respect for diversity means accepting and valuing differences in culture, looks, ability and beliefs.

questions.question: Which of these is a personal STRENGTH you might list when thinking about yourself?
options: I live in a big house
questions.memo: Personal strengths are qualities inside you, like loyalty or kindness — not possessions.

questions.question: Your interests, abilities and ____ all make up who you are.
questions.memo: Knowing your interests, abilities and potential helps you understand and value yourself.

questions.question: A friend says something unkind about your appearance. Which response protects your self-image without hurting them?
options: Calmly say it hurt you and that you value yourself
questions.expected: Calmly say it hurt you and that you value yourself
questions.memo: Assertively naming the hurt while still valuing yourself protects your self-image and the relationship.

questions.question: The way your family and friends treat you can influence your self-image.
questions.memo: Relationships with self, family and friends all shape how you see yourself.

questions.question: Which is a POSITIVE action that strengthens your self-image?
options: Setting a small goal and achieving it
questions.expected: Setting a small goal and achieving it
questions.memo: Achieving goals, however small, gives a sense of competence that strengthens self-image.

questions.question: Believing in your own abilities gives you self-____.
questions.memo: Self-confidence is trusting your own abilities; it grows from positive experiences and self-talk.

questions.question: Why is a healthy self-image important for a teenager?
options: It helps you make good choices and resist pressure
It guarantees you will be rich
It means you never feel sad
questions.expected: It helps you make good choices and resist pressure
questions.memo: A healthy self-image supports good decision-making and the confidence to resist harmful pressure.

questions.question: Putting other people down is a good way to feel better about yourself.
questions.memo: Tearing others down damages relationships and does not build a genuine, lasting self-image.

questions.question: Which sentence is an example of POSITIVE self-talk?
options: 'I can improve if I keep trying'
questions.expected: 'I can improve if I keep trying'
questions.memo: Positive self-talk focuses on growth and effort, which builds a healthy self-image.

questions.question: A new learner joins your class and seems shy. What helps THEIR self-image most?
options: Welcome them and introduce them to others
questions.expected: Welcome them and introduce them to others
questions.memo: Including and welcoming others shows respect and helps build their self-image.

questions.question: Accepting that you have both strengths and weaknesses is part of a healthy self-image.
questions.memo: Self-acceptance — owning both strengths and weaknesses — is central to a realistic, healthy self-image.

questions.question: Showing you value other people's worth is called respect for ____.
questions.memo: Respect for others means valuing their worth, feelings and differences.

questions.question: Which is the BEST long-term way to improve self-image?
options: Build real skills and treat yourself and others well
questions.expected: Build real skills and treat yourself and others well
questions.memo: Genuine self-image grows from real competence and respectful relationships, not from possessions or winning.

questions.question: Sort each action into whether it BUILDS UP or BREAKS DOWN self-image.
questions.expected: Praise and reaching goals build self-image; bullying and harsh self-criticism break it down.
questions.memo: Encouragement and achievement build self-image; cruelty and harsh self-criticism damage it.

LO.G7.DS.A2.title: Puberty and gender constructs
LO.G7.DS.A2.description: Development of the self in society (CAPS G7 T1) — Development of the self in society: Puberty and gender constructs.
LO.G7.DS.A2.strand: Development of the self in society · Term 1
LO.G7.DS.A2.caps_topic: Development of the self in society
LO.G7.DS.A2.recovery_strategy: Puberty brings physical and emotional changes; everyone changes at their own pace, and that is normal.

questions.question: What is puberty?
options: The stage when the body changes from a child's into an adult's
questions.expected: The stage when the body changes from a child's into an adult's
questions.memo: Puberty is the natural stage when the body matures from childhood toward adulthood.

questions.question: Everyone goes through puberty at exactly the same age.
questions.memo: Puberty starts and progresses at different ages for different people — there is no single 'correct' time.

questions.question: Which of these is a PHYSICAL change during puberty?
questions.memo: Physical changes in puberty include growth, body hair, and the body maturing — these are normal.

questions.question: Which of these is an EMOTIONAL change many teenagers notice during puberty?
questions.memo: Mood changes and stronger emotions are common emotional changes during puberty.

questions.question: The physical and emotional changes of puberty are completely ____.
questions.memo: These changes are a normal, healthy part of growing up that everyone experiences.

questions.question: It is respectful to tease someone about how their body is changing.
questions.memo: Teasing about body changes is disrespectful and harmful; we should respect our own and others' changes.

questions.question: A friend feels embarrassed about changes in their body. What is the kind, respectful response?
options: Reassure them that the changes are normal for everyone
Tell them something is wrong with them
questions.expected: Reassure them that the changes are normal for everyone
questions.memo: Reassurance and respect help a friend feel safe; the changes are normal for everyone.

questions.question: Ideas a society has about how boys and girls 'should' behave are called gender ____.
questions.memo: Gender constructs are society's ideas about how boys and girls should act — they are learned, not fixed.

questions.question: Boys are not allowed to cry or show emotion — this is a healthy rule.
questions.memo: The idea that boys must not show emotion is a harmful gender stereotype; everyone has feelings.

questions.question: Which statement challenges an unfair gender stereotype?
options: Both girls and boys can be leaders and carers
questions.expected: Both girls and boys can be leaders and carers
questions.memo: People of any gender can lead, care, cook or do science; rigid roles are unfair stereotypes.

questions.question: How do puberty changes affect relationships with friends and family?
options: Feelings and reactions may change, so communication matters more
questions.expected: Feelings and reactions may change, so communication matters more
questions.memo: Changing emotions can affect relationships, so honest communication and patience help.

questions.question: Keeping clean and looking after your body is important during puberty.
questions.memo: Good hygiene becomes especially important during puberty as the body changes.

questions.question: Accepting the changes in your body shows ____ for yourself.
questions.memo: Accepting your body's changes is a way of respecting yourself.

questions.question: Which is the healthiest attitude toward puberty?
options: It is a natural stage I can understand and accept
questions.expected: It is a natural stage I can understand and accept
questions.memo: Understanding and accepting puberty as natural leads to the healthiest attitude.

questions.question: Girls and boys both experience physical and emotional changes during puberty.
questions.memo: Both girls and boys go through physical and emotional changes, though some differ.

questions.question: Where can a teenager get trustworthy information about puberty?
options: A parent, teacher, nurse or reliable health book
Random comments online with no source
questions.expected: A parent, teacher, nurse or reliable health book
questions.memo: Trusted adults and reliable health sources give accurate information about puberty.

questions.question: A classmate says 'real men don't ask for help.' Why is this idea a problem?
options: It stops boys getting support they need
questions.expected: It stops boys getting support they need
questions.memo: This harmful gender construct discourages help-seeking, which can hurt mental and physical health.

questions.question: Appreciating and accepting yourself and others is part of growing up well.
questions.memo: Self-acceptance and accepting others are healthy parts of development during puberty.

questions.question: Sort each change into PHYSICAL or EMOTIONAL.
questions.expected: Growing taller and a deepening voice are physical; moodiness and self-consciousness are emotional.
questions.memo: Physical changes affect the body; emotional changes affect feelings and moods.

questions.question: Comparing your body to other people's can cause needless worry during puberty.
questions.memo: Everyone develops at their own pace, so comparing yourself to others often causes unnecessary worry.

LO.G7.DS.A3.title: Peer pressure
LO.G7.DS.A3.description: Development of the self in society (CAPS G7 T1) — Development of the self in society: Peer pressure.
LO.G7.DS.A3.strand: Development of the self in society · Term 1
LO.G7.DS.A3.caps_topic: Development of the self in society
LO.G7.DS.A3.recovery_strategy: Peer pressure is when others push you to act a certain way; being assertive lets you say no calmly.

questions.question: What is peer pressure?
options: Influence from people your own age to act in a certain way
questions.expected: Influence from people your own age to act in a certain way
questions.memo: Peer pressure is the influence that people of your own age group have on your choices and behaviour.

questions.question: Peer pressure is always negative.
questions.memo: Peer pressure can be positive (friends encouraging study or sport) or negative (pushing risky behaviour).

questions.question: Which is an example of NEGATIVE peer pressure?
options: Friends daring you to skip class
questions.expected: Friends daring you to skip class
questions.memo: Negative peer pressure pushes you toward harmful or risky behaviour like skipping class.

questions.question: Which is an example of POSITIVE peer pressure?
options: A friend who motivates you to join a study group
questions.expected: A friend who motivates you to join a study group
questions.memo: Positive peer pressure encourages healthy, helpful choices.

questions.question: Saying 'no' in a calm, confident and firm way is being ____.
questions.memo: Assertiveness means standing up for yourself calmly and confidently, without being aggressive.

questions.question: Friends pressure Lerato to bunk school. Which response is ASSERTIVE?
options: 'No thanks, I'm going to class' said calmly
Going along to avoid the fuss
questions.expected: 'No thanks, I'm going to class' said calmly
questions.memo: An assertive response is calm, clear and firm — neither aggressive nor giving in.

questions.question: Negotiation skills include being able to disagree in a constructive way.
questions.memo: Negotiation means working out a solution and being able to disagree respectfully and constructively.

questions.question: Peer pressure may push teenagers toward which risky behaviour?
questions.memo: Negative peer pressure can push toward substances, crime, unhealthy behaviour and bullying.

questions.question: If pressure becomes too much, it is wise to find ____.
questions.memo: Knowing where to find help — a trusted adult, counsellor or helpline — is an important coping skill.

questions.question: Who is a good person to ask for help with serious peer pressure?
options: A trusted teacher, parent or school counsellor
questions.expected: A trusted teacher, parent or school counsellor
questions.memo: Trusted adults like teachers, parents and counsellors can help you handle serious pressure.

questions.question: Giving in to negative peer pressure is the only way to keep friends.
questions.memo: Real friends respect your choices; you can keep good friends while refusing harmful pressure.

questions.question: What is the difference between being assertive and being aggressive?
options: Assertive is calm and firm; aggressive is hostile and forceful
questions.expected: Assertive is calm and firm; aggressive is hostile and forceful
questions.memo: Assertiveness respects everyone; aggression tries to dominate or harm.

questions.question: A friend keeps pushing you to share answers in a test. The BEST coping skill is to…
options: firmly refuse and explain it is cheating
questions.expected: firmly refuse and explain it is cheating
questions.memo: Refusing firmly and explaining your reason is an assertive, honest coping skill.

questions.question: Coping skills help you handle pressure without harming yourself or others.
questions.memo: Coping skills like assertiveness and seeking help manage pressure in healthy ways.

questions.question: Being able to influence others toward good choices is ____ peer pressure.
questions.memo: You can be a positive influence on your peers, encouraging good choices.

questions.question: Which sign suggests a friendship is unhealthy?
options: They only want you around if you do what they say
questions.expected: They only want you around if you do what they say
questions.memo: Conditional friendship that punishes your 'no' is a sign of unhealthy pressure.

questions.question: Sipho is dared to bully a younger learner to 'prove' he is cool. The responsible choice is to…
options: refuse and, if needed, report the bullying
do it once to fit in
questions.expected: refuse and, if needed, report the bullying
questions.memo: Refusing and reporting protects the younger learner and shows responsible courage.

questions.question: Practising what you will say in advance can make it easier to resist pressure.
questions.memo: Rehearsing a firm response ahead of time makes assertiveness easier in the moment.

questions.question: Put the steps for handling negative peer pressure in a sensible order.

items.text: Recognise the pressure is pushing you toward something harmful
Decide on your own values and what you want
Say no calmly and firmly (be assertive)
If it continues, walk away and find help

questions.expected: Recognise the pressure, decide your values, refuse assertively, then walk away and find help if needed.
questions.memo: First notice the pressure, know your own mind, refuse assertively, and seek help if it continues.

questions.question: Why are negotiation skills useful with peers?
options: They let you disagree and still keep respect
They force others to obey you
They help you win every fight
questions.expected: They let you disagree and still keep respect
questions.memo: Negotiation lets you disagree constructively while keeping the relationship respectful.

LO.G7.DS.A4.title: Personal diet and nutrition
LO.G7.DS.A4.description: Development of the self in society (CAPS G7 T1) — Development of the self in society: Personal diet and nutrition.
LO.G7.DS.A4.strand: Development of the self in society · Term 1
LO.G7.DS.A4.caps_topic: Development of the self in society
LO.G7.DS.A4.recovery_strategy: A balanced diet gives your body the right nutrients; small healthy swaps improve your eating.

questions.question: What does 'nutrition' refer to?
options: The food and nutrients your body needs to stay healthy
questions.expected: The food and nutrients your body needs to stay healthy
questions.memo: Nutrition is about the nutrients in food that the body needs to grow and stay healthy.

questions.question: A balanced diet includes a variety of food groups in the right amounts.
questions.memo: A balanced diet provides variety from all food groups in suitable amounts.

questions.question: Which factor can influence the food a person chooses?
options: Culture, cost and what is available
The day of the week only
questions.expected: Culture, cost and what is available
questions.memo: Diet choices are shaped by ecological, social, economic, cultural and political factors.

questions.question: Foods that give the body energy and help it grow are full of ____.
questions.memo: Nutrients (like protein, carbohydrates, vitamins) give energy and help the body grow and repair.

questions.question: Which is the healthier swap to improve a diet?
options: Fruit instead of sweets as a snack
More fizzy drinks instead of water
questions.expected: Fruit instead of sweets as a snack
questions.memo: Swapping sweets for fruit improves nutritional value — a simple, healthy change.

questions.question: Drinking water instead of sugary drinks is a good way to improve your diet.
questions.memo: Choosing water over sugary drinks reduces sugar intake and improves health.

questions.question: Why might two families eat very different meals?
options: Different cultures, budgets and what foods they can get
One family is better than the other
Food has no link to culture
questions.expected: Different cultures, budgets and what foods they can get
questions.memo: Culture, income and availability all shape what different families eat.

questions.question: Eating too much sugar and fatty food can lead to ____ problems.
questions.memo: Poor diet high in sugar and fat is linked to health problems like obesity and diabetes.

questions.question: Which is the BEST description of a plan for healthy eating habits?
options: Eat varied, balanced meals and limit junk food
questions.expected: Eat varied, balanced meals and limit junk food
questions.memo: A healthy-eating plan means variety, balance and limiting junk food.

questions.question: Cost is one economic factor that affects what people can eat.
questions.memo: Economic factors like cost and income strongly affect food choices.

questions.question: Fruit and vegetables are important mainly because they…
options: provide vitamins and fibre for good health
questions.expected: provide vitamins and fibre for good health
questions.memo: Fruit and vegetables supply vitamins, minerals and fibre that keep the body healthy.

questions.question: Naledi wants to improve her diet on a tight budget. A realistic step is to…
options: choose affordable, filling foods like beans, samp and seasonal veg
questions.expected: choose affordable, filling foods like beans, samp and seasonal veg
questions.memo: Affordable staples like beans, samp and seasonal vegetables improve nutrition on a budget.

questions.question: Eating a wide variety of foods helps you get different nutrients.
questions.memo: Variety helps ensure you get the full range of nutrients your body needs.

questions.question: A meal with protein, carbohydrates and vegetables is more ____ than chips alone.
questions.memo: Combining food groups makes a meal more balanced and nutritious.

questions.question: Which is a SOCIAL factor that influences diet?
options: Family traditions and what friends eat
questions.expected: Family traditions and what friends eat
questions.memo: Social factors include family customs and the eating habits of those around you.

questions.question: Healthy eating has no effect on your energy or concentration at school.
questions.memo: Good nutrition improves energy and concentration, helping you learn better.

questions.question: Skipping breakfast often leads to…
questions.memo: Skipping breakfast can lower energy and concentration during the school day.

questions.question: Sort each choice into HEALTHIER or LESS HEALTHY.

items.text: A packet of sweets for lunch

questions.expected: Fruit and water are healthier; fizzy drinks and sweets for lunch are less healthy.
questions.memo: Whole foods and water are healthier; sugary drinks and sweets are less nutritious.

questions.question: A 'personal diet plan' is useful because it…
options: helps you set realistic goals to eat better
forces everyone to eat the same
questions.expected: helps you set realistic goals to eat better
questions.memo: A personal plan sets realistic, individual goals to improve eating habits.

questions.question: Eating a healthy breakfast can improve your concentration at school.
questions.memo: A good breakfast gives steady energy that improves concentration and learning.

LO.G7.HE.A1.title: Substance abuse
LO.G7.HE.A1.description: Health, social & environmental responsibility (CAPS G7 T3) — Health, social and environmental responsibility: Substance abuse.
LO.G7.HE.A1.recovery_strategy: Substance abuse is harmful use of drugs or alcohol; knowing the risks helps you avoid it.

questions.question: What is substance abuse?
options: The harmful or unsafe use of drugs, alcohol or other substances
questions.expected: The harmful or unsafe use of drugs, alcohol or other substances
questions.memo: Substance abuse is using drugs, alcohol or other substances in harmful, unsafe ways.

questions.question: Alcohol and tobacco are examples of substances that can be abused.
questions.memo: Alcohol and tobacco, along with illegal drugs and some medicines, can be abused.

questions.question: Which is a possible SYMPTOM of substance abuse?
options: Sudden change in behaviour and dropping marks
questions.expected: Sudden change in behaviour and dropping marks
questions.memo: Warning signs include behaviour changes, falling marks, mood swings and withdrawal.

questions.question: Catching a problem early is called early ____.
questions.memo: Early detection means noticing the warning signs early so help can be given sooner.

questions.question: Which is a PERSONAL (intrapersonal) factor that may contribute to substance abuse?
questions.memo: Intrapersonal factors come from within, like low self-esteem, stress or curiosity.

questions.question: Which is an INTERPERSONAL factor that may contribute to substance abuse?
options: Pressure from friends who use substances
questions.expected: Pressure from friends who use substances
questions.memo: Interpersonal factors involve other people, like peer pressure or family use.

questions.question: Protective factors are things that lower the chance of substance abuse.
questions.memo: Protective factors — like good self-esteem, supportive family and hobbies — reduce the risk.

questions.question: Which is a PROTECTIVE factor against substance abuse?
questions.memo: Self-esteem, support, goals and healthy hobbies protect against substance abuse.

questions.question: Stopping a problem before it starts is called ____.
questions.memo: Prevention means taking steps to stop substance abuse before it begins.

questions.question: Substance abuse only affects the person using; it never affects family or friends.
questions.memo: Substance abuse harms the user and also affects family, friends and the community.

questions.question: A friend shows sudden mood swings, skips school and avoids old friends. These could be…
options: warning signs worth talking to a trusted adult about
questions.expected: warning signs worth talking to a trusted adult about
questions.memo: Such changes can be warning signs; the caring response is to involve a trusted adult.

questions.question: What is the healthiest way to deal with stress instead of using substances?
options: Exercise, talk to someone, or use a hobby
questions.expected: Exercise, talk to someone, or use a hobby
questions.memo: Healthy coping (exercise, talking, hobbies) handles stress without the harm of substances.

questions.question: Saying no to substances is easier when you have planned what to say.
questions.memo: Having a refusal plan ready makes it easier to say no in the moment.

questions.question: Substances that change how the brain and body work can cause ____.
questions.memo: Abused substances change brain and body function and can cause serious harm.

questions.question: Where can someone struggling with substance abuse find help?
options: A clinic, counsellor or helpline like SANCA
questions.expected: A clinic, counsellor or helpline like SANCA
questions.memo: Clinics, counsellors and organisations like SANCA offer help, care and support.

questions.question: Curiosity and wanting to fit in are reasons some young people try substances.
questions.memo: Curiosity and the wish to fit in are common reasons young people first try substances.

questions.question: Why is prevention better than treatment for substance abuse?
options: It stops the harm before it happens
It costs more and helps less
questions.expected: It stops the harm before it happens
questions.memo: Prevention avoids the harm altogether, which is better than treating it later.

questions.question: Sort each item into a RISK factor or a PROTECTIVE factor for substance abuse.
questions.expected: Low self-esteem and drug-using friends are risks; supportive family and healthy hobbies are protective.
questions.memo: Risk factors raise the chance of abuse; protective factors lower it.

questions.question: Which choice best reduces a teenager's likelihood of substance abuse?
options: Joining positive activities and building strong support
questions.expected: Joining positive activities and building strong support
questions.memo: Positive activities and supportive relationships are strong protective factors.

questions.question: It is brave, not weak, to ask for help with a substance-abuse problem.
questions.memo: Reaching out for help takes courage and is the first step toward recovery.

LO.G7.HE.A2.title: Environmental health
LO.G7.HE.A2.description: Health, social & environmental responsibility (CAPS G7 T3) — Health, social and environmental responsibility: Environmental health.
LO.G7.HE.A2.recovery_strategy: Environmental health means keeping our surroundings clean and safe so people stay healthy.

questions.question: What does 'environmental health' mean?
options: Keeping our surroundings clean and safe so people stay healthy
questions.expected: Keeping our surroundings clean and safe so people stay healthy
questions.memo: Environmental health is about keeping our surroundings clean and safe to protect people's health.

questions.question: Pollution and dirty water are examples of environmental health problems.
questions.memo: Pollution, dirty water, litter and poor sanitation are environmental health problems.

questions.question: Which is a LOCAL environmental health problem a community might face?
questions.memo: Litter, dumping, polluted water and poor sanitation are common local problems.

questions.question: A clear set of steps to solve a problem is called an action ____.
questions.memo: An action plan lists the steps a community or person will take to solve a problem.

questions.question: Which is a good community action to improve environmental health?
options: Organise a clean-up and recycle waste
questions.expected: Organise a clean-up and recycle waste
questions.memo: Clean-ups and recycling are positive actions that improve environmental health.

questions.question: Recycling helps reduce waste and protect the environment.
questions.memo: Recycling reduces waste sent to landfill and protects the environment.

questions.question: Why is clean water important for environmental health?
options: Water has no effect on health
questions.memo: Unsafe water spreads diseases like cholera, so clean water is vital for health.

questions.question: Working out the cause and steps of a problem uses problem-____ skills.
questions.memo: Problem-solving skills help you find causes and plan actions to fix a problem.

questions.question: An 'environmentally sound choice' is one that…
options: protects rather than harms the environment
questions.expected: protects rather than harms the environment
questions.memo: Environmentally sound choices protect the environment and reduce harm.

questions.question: One person's actions can never make a difference to the environment.
questions.memo: Individual actions add up; each person's choices do make a difference.

questions.question: Your area has a litter problem near the school. A good FIRST step in an action plan is to…
options: identify the problem and its causes
questions.expected: identify the problem and its causes
questions.memo: A good action plan starts by clearly identifying the problem and its causes.

questions.question: Which individual habit helps the environment most?
questions.memo: Reduce, reuse, recycle is a key individual habit that protects the environment.

questions.question: Poor sanitation, like blocked drains, can cause health problems in a community.
questions.memo: Poor sanitation spreads germs and disease, harming community health.

questions.question: Putting waste in the right bin instead of the street reduces ____.
questions.memo: Correct waste disposal reduces pollution and keeps the area healthier.

questions.question: A community project to clean a polluted stream is an example of…
questions.memo: Community clean-up projects show responsibility for environmental health.

questions.question: Put the steps of an environmental health action plan in order.

items.text: Find out what is causing it
Plan and carry out an action to fix it

questions.expected: Identify the problem, find the cause, take action, then check if it improved.
questions.memo: A sound action plan: identify, find the cause, act, then evaluate the result.

questions.question: Planting trees and keeping public spaces clean improve environmental health.
questions.memo: Greening and cleaning public spaces improve both the environment and people's health.

questions.question: Why should communities work TOGETHER on environmental health?
options: Shared effort solves big problems faster
questions.expected: Shared effort solves big problems faster
questions.memo: Working together pools effort and resources, solving environmental problems faster.

questions.question: Sort each action into HELPS the environment or HARMS it.
questions.expected: Recycling and picking up litter help; dumping waste and burning plastic harm.
questions.memo: Reducing waste and cleaning up help the environment; dumping and burning harm it.

questions.question: Saving water and electricity is part of caring for the environment.
questions.memo: Conserving water and electricity reduces waste and protects the environment.

LO.G7.HE.A3.title: Common diseases
LO.G7.HE.A3.description: Health, social & environmental responsibility (CAPS G7 T3) — Health, social and environmental responsibility: Common diseases.
LO.G7.HE.A3.recovery_strategy: Many common diseases can be treated or managed with the right care, diet and medicine.

questions.question: Which of these is a common disease covered in Grade 7 Life Orientation?
questions.memo: Common diseases studied include TB, diabetes, epilepsy, obesity, anorexia and HIV and AIDS.

questions.question: Diabetes is a condition that affects how the body controls blood sugar.
questions.memo: Diabetes affects how the body manages blood sugar (glucose).

questions.question: What is TB (tuberculosis) mainly an illness of?
questions.memo: TB is an infectious disease that mainly affects the lungs but is treatable with medication.

questions.question: A disease you can pass to others is described as ____.
questions.memo: Infectious (communicable) diseases, like TB, can spread from person to person.

questions.question: Which factor can contribute to many common diseases?
options: Poor eating habits and physical inactivity
questions.expected: Poor eating habits and physical inactivity
questions.memo: Causes include social, economic and environmental factors plus poor diet, inactivity, alcohol and tobacco.

questions.question: HIV and AIDS can be managed so that a person lives a long, healthy life.
questions.memo: With treatment, diet and a positive attitude, people with HIV can live long, healthy lives.

questions.question: Anorexia is best described as…
options: an eating disorder where a person eats too little
questions.expected: an eating disorder where a person eats too little
questions.memo: Anorexia is a serious eating disorder involving extreme food restriction.

questions.question: Epilepsy is a condition that affects the…
questions.memo: Epilepsy affects the brain and can cause seizures, but it can be managed with medication.

questions.question: Obesity is linked to eating too much unhealthy food and too little ____.
questions.memo: Obesity is linked to poor diet and lack of physical activity.

questions.question: People living with a chronic disease deserve care, support and no discrimination.
questions.memo: People with chronic illnesses deserve care and support, not stigma or discrimination.

questions.question: Where can a family find reliable health information and services?
options: A clinic, hospital or qualified health worker
questions.expected: A clinic, hospital or qualified health worker
questions.memo: Clinics, hospitals and health workers are reliable sources of health information and services.

questions.question: A good strategy for living well with a chronic disease like diabetes is to…
options: follow treatment, eat well and stay active
hide the condition and avoid care
questions.expected: follow treatment, eat well and stay active
questions.memo: Managing a chronic disease means following treatment, eating well and staying active.

questions.question: Tobacco and alcohol use can increase the risk of several diseases.
questions.memo: Tobacco and alcohol use raise the risk of many diseases, including lung and heart disease.

questions.question: Care and ____ help people cope with a serious illness.
questions.memo: Care and support help people cope physically and emotionally with illness.

questions.question: Why is early treatment of TB important?
options: It cures the person and stops it spreading to others
questions.expected: It cures the person and stops it spreading to others
questions.memo: Early TB treatment cures the patient and prevents spread to others.

questions.question: Which lifestyle choice helps PREVENT many common diseases?
questions.memo: A healthy diet and regular activity help prevent many common diseases.

questions.question: You can tell exactly who is living with HIV just by looking at them.
questions.memo: You cannot tell who has HIV by appearance; assuming so causes unfair stigma.

questions.question: Sort each item into a CAUSE/RISK or a HEALTHY PREVENTION for common diseases.
questions.expected: Smoking and junk food are risks; exercise and a balanced diet help prevent disease.
questions.memo: Smoking and poor diet raise disease risk; exercise and balanced eating help prevent it.

questions.question: A classmate has epilepsy. The kind and correct attitude is to…
options: treat them normally and know how to help if a seizure happens
questions.expected: treat them normally and know how to help if a seizure happens
questions.memo: People with epilepsy should be treated normally; knowing basic first aid helps in a seizure.

questions.question: Going for regular check-ups can catch many diseases early.
questions.memo: Regular health check-ups help detect diseases early, when they are easier to treat.

LO.G7.CR.A1.title: Human rights in the Constitution
LO.G7.CR.A1.description: Constitutional rights & responsibilities (CAPS G7 T2) — Constitutional rights and responsibilities: Human rights in the Constitution.
LO.G7.CR.A1.recovery_strategy: Every right in the Constitution comes with a responsibility to respect the same right in others.

questions.question: What is the Constitution of South Africa?
options: The highest law that sets out everyone's rights
questions.expected: The highest law that sets out everyone's rights
questions.memo: The Constitution is South Africa's highest law; the Bill of Rights lists the rights of all people.

questions.question: The Bill of Rights protects the rights of everyone in South Africa.
questions.memo: The Bill of Rights in the Constitution protects the rights of all people in the country.

questions.question: Which is a human right in the Constitution?
questions.memo: Rights include education, equality, dignity and safety — not the 'right' to harm others.

questions.question: Every right comes with a ____ to respect the same right in others.
questions.memo: Rights carry responsibilities — you must respect others' rights as you claim your own.

questions.question: You have the right to education. What is your matching RESPONSIBILITY?
options: Attend school and let others learn too
questions.expected: Attend school and let others learn too
questions.memo: The responsibility that matches the right to education is to attend and not stop others learning.

questions.question: Human rights apply only to adults, not to children.
questions.memo: Human rights apply to everyone, including children, who also have special protections.

questions.question: The right to equality means…
options: everyone is treated fairly and without unfair discrimination
some people are above the law
boys have more rights than girls
questions.expected: everyone is treated fairly and without unfair discrimination
questions.memo: Equality means fair treatment for all and protection from unfair discrimination.

questions.question: The right to be treated with respect and worth is the right to human ____.
questions.memo: Human dignity is the right to be valued and treated with respect.

questions.question: Someone says hurtful things about a classmate's religion. Which right is being disrespected?
questions.memo: Mocking someone's religion disrespects their freedom of religion and dignity.

questions.question: Respecting human rights helps build a fair and peaceful society.
questions.memo: When everyone respects rights, society becomes fairer and more peaceful.

questions.question: Applying your rights responsibly means…
options: using your rights without taking away others' rights
questions.expected: using your rights without taking away others' rights
questions.memo: Responsible use of rights respects the equal rights of everyone else.

questions.question: The right to freedom of speech allows you to…
questions.memo: Freedom of speech lets you express views, but not to harm, threaten or spread hate.

questions.question: Freedom of speech means you can say anything, even hateful threats.
questions.memo: Freedom of speech has limits; it does not protect hate speech, threats or incitement to harm.

questions.question: A document inside the Constitution listing our rights is the Bill of ____.
questions.memo: The Bill of Rights is the part of the Constitution that lists fundamental rights.

questions.question: Why is it important that everyone knows their rights?
options: So they can claim them and respect others' rights
So they can break the law
questions.expected: So they can claim them and respect others' rights
questions.memo: Knowing your rights lets you stand up for them and respect the rights of others.

questions.question: Children have the right to be protected from abuse and neglect.
questions.memo: The Constitution gives children special rights, including protection from abuse and neglect.

questions.question: Which action shows you are taking RESPONSIBILITY for others' rights?
options: Standing up against unfair treatment of a classmate
questions.expected: Standing up against unfair treatment of a classmate
questions.memo: Defending others against unfair treatment is taking responsibility for their rights.

questions.question: Match each RIGHT with its matching RESPONSIBILITY by ordering the responsibilities to fit Right 1→4.

items.text: (for Right to education) Attend school and respect others' learning
(for Right to safety) Do not harm or threaten others
(for Right to a clean environment) Do not litter or pollute
(for Freedom of religion) Respect others' beliefs

questions.expected: Education→attend and respect learning; safety→do not harm; environment→do not pollute; religion→respect beliefs.
questions.memo: Each right has a matching responsibility: respect the same right in everyone else.

questions.question: The best summary of rights and responsibilities is…
options: my rights end where another person's rights begin
I can do anything I like
questions.expected: my rights end where another person's rights begin
questions.memo: Your freedom is balanced by respect for everyone else's equal rights.

questions.question: The Constitution protects people of all races, genders and religions equally.
questions.memo: The Constitution protects everyone equally, regardless of race, gender or religion.

LO.G7.CR.A2.title: Fair play in sport
LO.G7.CR.A2.description: Constitutional rights & responsibilities (CAPS G7 T2) — Constitutional rights and responsibilities: Fair play in sport.
LO.G7.CR.A2.recovery_strategy: Fair play means respecting the rules, your opponents and the referee, win or lose.

questions.question: What does 'fair play' in sport mean?
options: Playing honestly and respecting the rules and others
questions.expected: Playing honestly and respecting the rules and others
questions.memo: Fair play means honesty, respecting the rules, opponents and officials, win or lose.

questions.question: Respect for your opponents is part of fair play.
questions.memo: Respecting opponents, teammates and officials is central to fair play.

questions.question: Which action shows fair play?
questions.memo: Helping an opponent and showing respect are clear signs of fair play.

questions.question: Believing your teammates will do their part is called ____.
questions.memo: Trust in teammates is a value that helps a team play and work well together.

questions.question: Your team loses a close game. The fair-play response is to…
questions.memo: Accepting defeat graciously and congratulating winners shows fair play.

questions.question: Respect for difference means valuing players of all backgrounds and abilities.
questions.memo: Fair play includes respect for difference — valuing all players regardless of background or ability.

questions.question: Why are rules important in sport?
options: They keep the game fair and safe for everyone
They make sport boring on purpose
questions.expected: They keep the game fair and safe for everyone
questions.memo: Rules keep sport fair and safe, so everyone has an equal chance.

questions.question: A teammate wants to cheat to win. The fair-play choice is to…
options: refuse and remind them to play honestly
questions.expected: refuse and remind them to play honestly
questions.memo: Refusing to cheat and encouraging honesty upholds fair play and the team's integrity.

questions.question: Good sportspersons show respect even when they ____.
questions.memo: True sportsmanship shows respect in both victory and defeat.

questions.question: Mocking a weaker player is acceptable as long as your team wins.
questions.memo: Mocking others is never fair play, regardless of the result.

questions.question: Fair play teaches values that are useful…
options: in everyday life, not just on the field
questions.expected: in everyday life, not just on the field
questions.memo: Values like honesty and respect from sport carry into everyday life.

questions.question: Which is an example of UNFAIR play?
questions.memo: Intentionally harming an opponent is a serious breach of fair play.

questions.question: Accepting a referee's decision, even when you disagree, shows good values.
questions.memo: Respecting officials' decisions, even in disagreement, is part of fair play.

questions.question: Playing by the rules and being honest shows good ____.
questions.memo: Honesty and rule-following reflect good personal values in sport.

questions.question: How can a captain encourage fair play in a team?
options: Set an example of honesty and respect
questions.expected: Set an example of honesty and respect
questions.memo: Leaders set the tone; modelling honesty and respect encourages team fair play.

questions.question: Trust and respect help a team work well together.
questions.memo: Trust and respect among players build teamwork and performance.

questions.question: Including a player who is new or less skilled shows…
options: respect for difference and good sportsmanship
questions.expected: respect for difference and good sportsmanship
questions.memo: Including all players shows respect for difference and good sportsmanship.

questions.question: Sort each behaviour into FAIR PLAY or UNFAIR PLAY.
questions.expected: Handshakes and respecting calls are fair play; tripping and lying are unfair play.
questions.memo: Fair play is honest and respectful; unfair play cheats or harms.

questions.question: The deeper purpose of fair play is to…
questions.memo: Fair play builds character, respect and trust that last beyond the game.

questions.question: Cheering on your own team while still respecting opponents is good sportsmanship.
questions.memo: You can support your team enthusiastically while still respecting the other side.

LO.G7.CR.A3.title: Dealing with abuse
LO.G7.CR.A3.description: Constitutional rights & responsibilities (CAPS G7 T2) — Constitutional rights and responsibilities: Dealing with abuse.
LO.G7.CR.A3.recovery_strategy: Abuse is never the victim's fault; knowing the warning signs and where to get help keeps you safe.

questions.question: What is abuse?
options: When someone harms, hurts or mistreats another person
questions.expected: When someone harms, hurts or mistreats another person
questions.memo: Abuse is when someone harms, hurts or mistreats another person physically, emotionally or otherwise.

questions.question: Abuse can happen between adults and children, or between peers.
questions.memo: Abuse can occur in many relationships, including adult–child and peer–peer.

questions.question: Which is a sign of a threatening or risky situation?
options: Someone tries to get you alone and makes you uncomfortable
A friend invites you to study
A teacher gives a fair test
questions.expected: Someone tries to get you alone and makes you uncomfortable
questions.memo: Feeling unsafe, pressured or isolated by someone can be a warning sign of a risky situation.

questions.question: If something feels wrong or unsafe, you should tell a ____ adult.
questions.memo: Telling a trusted adult is a key way to protect yourself in risky situations.

questions.question: Abuse is always the victim's fault.
questions.memo: Abuse is never the victim's fault; the responsibility lies with the person who chooses to abuse.

questions.question: How can abuse affect a person's health and relationships?
options: It can harm their emotions, trust and wellbeing
It has no effect at all
questions.expected: It can harm their emotions, trust and wellbeing
questions.memo: Abuse can deeply harm emotional health, trust and relationships.

questions.question: Why is communication important in healthy relationships?
options: It helps solve problems without violence
questions.expected: It helps solve problems without violence
questions.memo: Open communication promotes healthy, non-violent relationships.

questions.question: A place where abuse victims can get help and safety is a place of ____.
questions.memo: Places of protection (clinics, police, shelters, helplines) offer safety and help to victims.

questions.question: You should keep abuse a secret to avoid trouble.
questions.memo: Keeping abuse secret allows it to continue; telling a trusted adult is the safe choice.

questions.question: Lerato's older neighbour keeps touching her in a way that feels wrong. What should she do?
options: Tell a trusted adult and seek help immediately
Keep quiet and hope it stops
questions.expected: Tell a trusted adult and seek help immediately
questions.memo: She should tell a trusted adult straight away; it is not her fault and help is available.

questions.question: Which is a place victims of abuse can contact for help?
questions.memo: Organisations like Childline and the police help and protect victims of abuse.

questions.question: Bullying by peers is a form of abuse.
questions.memo: Repeated bullying that harms or intimidates someone is a form of abuse.

questions.question: How can you protect yourself from threatening situations?
options: Stay aware, avoid being isolated, and tell someone you trust
questions.expected: Stay aware, avoid being isolated, and tell someone you trust
questions.memo: Awareness, avoiding isolation and telling a trusted person help protect you.

questions.question: Hurting someone with words, like constant insults, is ____ abuse.
questions.memo: Emotional abuse uses words and behaviour, like insults and threats, to harm someone.

questions.question: A friend tells you they are being abused at home. The best response is to…
options: listen, believe them and help them tell a trusted adult
promise to keep it a total secret
tell them it is their fault
questions.expected: listen, believe them and help them tell a trusted adult
questions.memo: Listen, believe, and help them reach a trusted adult or helpline — do not keep dangerous secrets.

questions.question: Reporting abuse can help stop it and protect the victim.
questions.memo: Reporting abuse to trusted adults or authorities can stop it and protect the victim.

questions.question: Which feeling might warn you that a situation is unsafe?
options: A strong gut feeling that something is wrong
questions.expected: A strong gut feeling that something is wrong
questions.memo: Trusting a strong 'something is wrong' feeling can help keep you safe.

questions.question: Put the steps for responding to a risky or abusive situation in order.

items.text: Recognise the situation feels threatening or wrong
Remove yourself from danger if you safely can
Tell a trusted adult what happened

questions.expected: Recognise the danger, get to safety, tell a trusted adult, then get ongoing support.
questions.memo: Recognise, get safe, tell a trusted adult, and seek ongoing help.

questions.question: Healthy, non-violent relationships are built on…
questions.memo: Respect, trust and communication are the foundation of healthy, non-violent relationships.

questions.question: Asking for help after abuse is a sign of strength, not weakness.
questions.memo: Seeking help takes courage and is the right step toward safety and healing.

LO.G7.CR.A4.title: Oral traditions and scriptures of religions
LO.G7.CR.A4.description: Constitutional rights & responsibilities (CAPS G7 T2) — Constitutional rights and responsibilities: Oral traditions and scriptures of religions.
LO.G7.CR.A4.recovery_strategy: Each major religion passes on its values through stories, oral traditions and sacred writings.

questions.question: What are 'oral traditions' in religion?
options: Stories and teachings passed on by word of mouth
questions.expected: Stories and teachings passed on by word of mouth
questions.memo: Oral traditions are teachings and stories passed down by speaking, from generation to generation.

questions.question: Scriptures are the sacred writings of a religion.
questions.memo: Scriptures are a religion's sacred or holy writings.

questions.question: Which is a major religion practised in South Africa?
questions.memo: Major religions in South Africa include Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Buddhism and African religion.

questions.question: The sacred text of Islam is the…
questions.memo: The Qur'an is the holy scripture of Islam.

questions.question: The sacred text central to Judaism is the…
questions.memo: The Torah is a central sacred text in Judaism.

questions.question: African religion often passes on values through stories, proverbs and ____ traditions.
questions.memo: African religion strongly uses oral traditions — stories, proverbs and spoken teachings.

questions.question: Different religions can teach similar values, like kindness and respect.
questions.memo: Many religions share values such as kindness, honesty, respect and caring for others.

questions.question: Why do religions use stories and scriptures?
options: To teach values and guide how people live
questions.expected: To teach values and guide how people live
questions.memo: Stories and scriptures pass on values and guidance for living well.

questions.question: Treating people of other religions with ____ helps everyone live in peace.
questions.memo: Respecting other religions promotes peace and tolerance in a diverse society.

questions.question: The Bhagavad Gita and Vedas are sacred texts associated with…
questions.memo: The Vedas and Bhagavad Gita are sacred Hindu scriptures.

questions.question: It is respectful to learn about religions different from your own.
questions.memo: Learning about other religions builds understanding and respect.

questions.question: A classmate follows a different religion from you. The respectful attitude is to…
options: be curious and respectful of their beliefs
tell them their religion is wrong
questions.expected: be curious and respectful of their beliefs
questions.memo: Respect and openness toward different beliefs build a tolerant society.

questions.question: Buddhism's teachings are often linked to the…
questions.memo: Buddhism follows the teachings of the Buddha, often shared through stories and texts.

questions.question: Sacred stories are often passed from ____ to grandchildren.
questions.memo: Oral traditions pass through generations, often from grandparents to grandchildren.

questions.question: Respecting religious diversity is part of respecting human rights.
questions.memo: Freedom of religion is a constitutional right; respecting diversity upholds it.

questions.question: How do oral traditions and scriptures help a community?
options: They pass on shared values, identity and guidance
questions.expected: They pass on shared values, identity and guidance
questions.memo: They give a community shared values, identity and guidance across generations.

questions.question: Sort each sacred text with its religion by ordering the texts to match Religion 1→4.
questions.memo: Each major religion has its own sacred scriptures.

questions.question: All religions must be the same for people to live together peacefully.
questions.memo: People of different religions can live peacefully together through mutual respect, not sameness.

questions.question: The MAIN value most religions encourage toward others is…
questions.memo: Compassion and respect for others are values shared across the major religions.

questions.question: Freedom of religion means people may follow the faith of their choice, or none.
questions.memo: The Constitution protects freedom of religion, including the choice to follow no religion.

LO.G7.WW.A1.title: Reading, studying and memory skills
LO.G7.WW.A1.description: World of work (CAPS G7 T2) — World of work: Reading, studying and memory skills.
LO.G7.WW.A1.recovery_strategy: Reading with understanding and using memory tricks helps you study and remember more.

questions.question: Why is reading with understanding important for studying?
options: It helps you learn and remember information
It has no effect on marks
questions.expected: It helps you learn and remember information
questions.memo: Reading with understanding helps you learn, remember and apply information across subjects.

questions.question: Reading for enjoyment can also improve your vocabulary and skills.
questions.memo: Reading for pleasure builds vocabulary, comprehension and general knowledge.

questions.question: Which is a good MEMORY skill for studying?
options: Repeating and testing yourself on key facts
questions.expected: Repeating and testing yourself on key facts
questions.memo: Active recall — testing yourself — and repetition strengthen memory.

questions.question: The ability to bring information back to mind is called ____.
questions.memo: Recall is being able to retrieve information from memory when you need it.

questions.question: Which study habit helps you concentrate best?
options: A quiet space with no distractions
Studying while walking in a crowd
questions.expected: A quiet space with no distractions
questions.memo: A quiet, distraction-free space helps concentration and learning.

questions.question: Making a summary in your own words helps you understand and remember.
questions.memo: Summarising in your own words deepens understanding and aids memory.

questions.question: Which is a memory aid that links new facts to something familiar?
questions.memo: Mnemonics and rhymes link new information to familiar patterns, aiding recall.

questions.question: Going over work again to keep it fresh is called ____.
questions.memo: Revision means reviewing work regularly so it stays in memory.

questions.question: Sipho reads a page once and forgets it by the next day. A better strategy is to…
options: review and self-test over several days
questions.expected: review and self-test over several days
questions.memo: Spacing revision and self-testing over days greatly improves long-term memory.

questions.question: Cramming everything the night before is the best way to remember long-term.
questions.memo: Cramming may help short-term, but spaced revision over time is far better for lasting memory.

questions.question: Reading for understanding means you should…
options: think about the meaning, not just the words
questions.expected: think about the meaning, not just the words
questions.memo: Reading for understanding focuses on meaning, not just decoding words.

questions.question: Which tool helps organise ideas visually for memory?
questions.memo: Mind maps organise ideas visually, helping understanding and recall.

questions.question: Getting enough sleep helps your brain remember what you studied.
questions.memo: Sleep helps the brain consolidate memories, improving recall.

questions.question: Asking yourself questions about a text is called active ____.
questions.memo: Active reading — questioning the text — improves comprehension and memory.

questions.question: Why does reading widely help in many subjects?
options: It builds vocabulary and background knowledge
questions.expected: It builds vocabulary and background knowledge
questions.memo: Wide reading builds vocabulary and knowledge that help across all subjects.

questions.question: Highlighting and making notes can help you focus on key points.
questions.memo: Highlighting and note-making focus attention on the most important points.

questions.question: Which is the BEST first step when studying a new chapter?
options: Skim the headings to get an overview
questions.expected: Skim the headings to get an overview
questions.memo: Skimming headings first gives an overview that makes detailed reading easier.

questions.question: Put these study steps in an effective order.

items.text: Skim the headings for an overview
Summarise the key points in your own words

questions.expected: Skim, read for understanding, summarise, then self-test.
questions.memo: Overview first, then read deeply, summarise, and test your recall.

questions.question: Good reading and study skills are important because they…
options: help you succeed in school and future work
questions.expected: help you succeed in school and future work
questions.memo: Strong reading and study skills support success in school and in the world of work.

questions.question: Taking short breaks during long study sessions can help you focus better.
questions.memo: Short, planned breaks help the brain rest and keep concentration high.

LO.G7.WW.A2.title: Career fields
LO.G7.WW.A2.description: World of work (CAPS G7 T2) — World of work: Career fields.
LO.G7.WW.A2.recovery_strategy: A career field groups related jobs; each needs certain subjects, interests and training.

questions.question: What is a 'career field'?
options: A group of related jobs and careers
questions.expected: A group of related jobs and careers
questions.memo: A career field is a group of related jobs that share interests, skills or subjects.

questions.question: Different career fields need different school subjects.
questions.memo: Each career field tends to require certain school subjects and skills.

questions.question: Which subjects are usually important for a career in HEALTH (like nursing)?
questions.memo: Health careers usually require Life Sciences and related science subjects.

questions.question: The things you are good at are your ____.
questions.memo: Abilities are what you can do well; matching them to a field helps you choose a career.

questions.question: Why should you think about your INTERESTS when choosing a career field?
options: You are more likely to enjoy and succeed at work you find interesting
questions.expected: You are more likely to enjoy and succeed at work you find interesting
questions.memo: Matching interests to a field makes work more enjoyable and sustainable.

questions.question: A career field has its own challenges as well as opportunities.
questions.memo: Each field offers opportunities but also challenges to consider before choosing.

questions.question: Which describes the 'work environment' of a career?
options: Where and how the work is done
The colour of the building only
questions.expected: Where and how the work is done
questions.memo: Work environment is the setting and conditions in which a job is done.

questions.question: Engineering and building careers usually need which subject?
questions.memo: Engineering and technical careers usually require Mathematics and sciences.

questions.question: How long you must study for a career is its ____ of study.
questions.memo: Duration of study is the length of training or education a career requires.

questions.question: You should think about the requirements of a career before choosing it.
questions.memo: Knowing the subjects, schooling and skills a career needs helps you plan and choose wisely.

questions.question: Where can you find information about careers and study options?
options: Career guidance services, websites and counsellors
questions.expected: Career guidance services, websites and counsellors
questions.memo: Career guidance, reliable websites and counsellors are good sources of career and study information.

questions.question: Naledi loves helping people and is strong in Life Sciences. A suitable field could be…
options: health care, like nursing or medicine
questions.expected: health care, like nursing or medicine
questions.memo: Matching her interest in helping people and her science strength points to health care.

questions.question: Some careers need university; others need a college diploma or apprenticeship.
questions.memo: Different careers need different paths — university, college diplomas or apprenticeships.

questions.question: Jobs in farming, food and nature are in the ____ career field.
questions.memo: Agricultural careers deal with farming, food production and natural resources.

questions.question: Why is it useful to explore career fields in Grade 7?
options: It helps you plan subjects and goals early
It is too early to matter
questions.expected: It helps you plan subjects and goals early
questions.memo: Exploring fields early helps you plan subject choices and set goals.

questions.question: The only thing that matters when choosing a career is how much money it pays.
questions.memo: Pay matters, but so do interests, abilities, work environment and opportunities.

questions.question: Which pairing of interest and field makes the best sense?
questions.memo: Good career choices align genuine interests and abilities with the field's demands.

questions.question: Sort each career into the BEST-matching field.
questions.expected: Nurse and doctor are health careers; civil engineer and electrician are engineering/technical.
questions.memo: Careers group into fields by the kind of work and subjects they share.

questions.question: Considering 'opportunities within a field' means looking at…
options: the chances to find work and grow in that field
questions.expected: the chances to find work and grow in that field
questions.memo: Opportunities mean the availability of jobs and room to advance in a field.

questions.question: It is fine to be interested in more than one career field at this stage.
questions.memo: Exploring several fields is healthy in Grade 7; you narrow your choices over time.

LO.G7.WW.A3.title: Career simulation and the value of work
LO.G7.WW.A3.description: World of work (CAPS G7 T2) — World of work: Career simulation and the value of work.
LO.G7.WW.A3.recovery_strategy: Work meets our needs and gives purpose; every career has its own tools, dress and requirements.

questions.question: What is the 'value of work' in a person's life?
options: Work helps meet needs and gives purpose and dignity
questions.expected: Work helps meet needs and gives purpose and dignity
questions.memo: Work helps fulfil personal needs and gives purpose, dignity and a sense of contribution.

questions.question: A 'dress code' is the kind of clothing suitable for a particular job.
questions.memo: A dress code is the expected clothing for a job, like a uniform or smart wear.

questions.question: Which tools would a CARPENTER most likely use?
questions.memo: Each career uses particular tools; a carpenter uses a saw, hammer and tape.

questions.question: The place where a person does their job is their place of ____.
questions.memo: The place of employment is where the work happens — office, hospital, site, etc.

questions.question: Why does work help fulfil personal needs?
options: It can provide income, skills and a sense of achievement
questions.expected: It can provide income, skills and a sense of achievement
questions.memo: Work provides income to meet needs, plus skills, achievement and self-worth.

questions.question: Different careers require different personality characteristics.
questions.memo: Careers suit different personalities; for example, a counsellor needs patience and empathy.

questions.question: A nurse's typical work environment includes…
questions.memo: A nurse usually works in a clinic or hospital, caring for patients.

questions.question: Which personality trait suits a career as a TEACHER?
questions.memo: Teaching suits patient, communicative people who enjoy helping others learn.

questions.question: Jobs that are similar to one another are called ____ careers.
questions.memo: Related careers share similar tasks, skills or fields.

questions.question: Knowing the school subjects a career needs helps you prepare for it.
questions.memo: Knowing the required subjects lets you choose and prepare for a career path.

questions.question: A 'career simulation' activity means you…
options: pretend to do a real career to learn what it involves
questions.expected: pretend to do a real career to learn what it involves
questions.memo: A career simulation lets you role-play a job to understand its tasks, tools and requirements.

questions.question: Why is it useful to learn a career's requirements before Grade 9?
options: So you can choose the right subjects in time
questions.expected: So you can choose the right subjects in time
questions.memo: Knowing requirements early helps you choose suitable subjects in Grade 10.

questions.question: Work can give a person a sense of dignity and self-worth.
questions.memo: Beyond income, work provides dignity, purpose and self-worth.

questions.question: A doctor or electrician must meet the schooling ____ for that career.
questions.memo: Requirements are the schooling, subjects and training a career demands.

questions.question: Which best shows the 'value of work in fulfilling potential'?
options: A person using their talents in a job they find meaningful
A person doing nothing all day
questions.expected: A person using their talents in a job they find meaningful
questions.memo: Meaningful work lets people use their talents and reach their potential.

questions.question: Every job, no matter how simple, has dignity and value.
questions.memo: All honest work has dignity and contributes value to society.

questions.question: Which is part of exploring a career through simulation?
options: Finding out its tools, dress code and where to study
questions.expected: Finding out its tools, dress code and where to study
questions.memo: A simulation explores a career's tools, dress code, environment and study path.

questions.question: Match each worker with their typical tool by ordering the tools to fit Worker 1→4.
questions.memo: Each career uses particular tools suited to its work.

questions.question: The MAIN reason to research a career before choosing it is to…
options: make an informed choice that fits you
questions.expected: make an informed choice that fits you
questions.memo: Researching a career helps you make an informed choice that suits your interests and abilities.

questions.question: Honest work in any career can give a person dignity and purpose.
questions.memo: All honest work has dignity and can give a person purpose and self-worth.

LO.G8.DS.A1.title: Self-concept and self-motivation
LO.G8.DS.A1.description: Development of the self in society (CAPS G8 T1) — Development of the self in society: Self-concept and self-motivation.
LO.G8.DS.A1.strand: Development of the self in society · Term 1
LO.G8.DS.A1.caps_topic: Development of the self in society
LO.G8.DS.A1.recovery_strategy: Your self-concept is built by many influences; positive self-talk keeps you motivated.

questions.question: What is 'self-concept'?
options: The overall idea you have about who you are
questions.expected: The overall idea you have about who you are
questions.memo: Self-concept is the overall picture and understanding you have of yourself.

questions.question: Self-motivation means pushing yourself to act without needing others to force you.
questions.memo: Self-motivation is the inner drive to act and reach goals without outside pressure.

questions.question: Which factor can INFLUENCE self-concept formation?
options: Family, friends, media, culture and religion
questions.expected: Family, friends, media, culture and religion
questions.memo: Self-concept is shaped by media, environment, friends, family, culture, religion and community.

questions.question: Encouraging yourself with kind, hopeful words is called positive self-____.
questions.memo: Positive self-talk uses encouraging words to build confidence and motivation.

questions.question: Which is an example of POSITIVE self-talk?
options: 'I worked hard and I can improve'
questions.expected: 'I worked hard and I can improve'
questions.memo: Positive self-talk focuses on effort and growth, boosting motivation.

questions.question: Each person is unique, with their own mix of strengths and qualities.
questions.memo: Individuality and uniqueness mean everyone has their own strengths and qualities.

questions.question: How can media influence a teenager's self-concept?
options: It can set unrealistic ideals to compare against
questions.expected: It can set unrealistic ideals to compare against
questions.memo: Media can present unrealistic ideals; comparing yourself to them can harm self-concept.

questions.question: Reaching a goal you set gives you a sense of personal ____.
questions.memo: Personal achievements strengthen self-concept and self-motivation.

questions.question: A strategy to EXTEND your personal potential is to…
options: set goals and keep learning new skills
questions.expected: set goals and keep learning new skills
questions.memo: Setting goals and learning new skills helps you extend your potential.

questions.question: Comparing yourself constantly to others usually strengthens self-concept.
questions.memo: Constant comparison often damages self-concept; focusing on your own growth is healthier.

questions.question: Thandi failed a test and thinks 'I'm stupid.' A healthier, motivating thought is…
options: 'I can study differently and do better next time'
questions.expected: 'I can study differently and do better next time'
questions.memo: Reframing setbacks as chances to improve protects self-concept and keeps motivation alive.

questions.question: Which is an INTERNAL source of motivation?
options: Personal pride in doing your best
questions.expected: Personal pride in doing your best
questions.memo: Internal (intrinsic) motivation comes from within, like pride and personal satisfaction.

questions.question: Your culture and religion can be part of how you see yourself.
questions.memo: Culture and religion are among the influences that shape self-concept.

questions.question: Believing you can improve with effort is called a growth ____.
questions.memo: A growth mindset is the belief that ability can grow with effort and practice.

questions.question: Why is self-motivation important for success?
options: It keeps you working toward goals even when it is hard
questions.expected: It keeps you working toward goals even when it is hard
questions.memo: Self-motivation keeps you pursuing goals through difficulties.

questions.question: Supportive friends and family can strengthen a positive self-concept.
questions.memo: Encouraging relationships help build a healthy, positive self-concept.

questions.question: Which habit best builds long-term self-motivation?
options: Setting small goals and celebrating progress
Waiting for others to push you
Giving up at the first setback
questions.expected: Setting small goals and celebrating progress
questions.memo: Small goals and recognising progress build lasting self-motivation.

questions.question: Sort each statement into POSITIVE or NEGATIVE self-talk.
questions.expected: Learning from mistakes and improving are positive; 'always fail' and 'no point' are negative.
questions.memo: Positive self-talk builds motivation; negative self-talk drains it.

questions.question: Put the steps for staying self-motivated toward a goal in order.

items.text: Work on the steps and track progress
Reward yourself and set the next goal

questions.expected: Set a goal, break it down, work and track progress, then reward yourself and continue.
questions.memo: Self-motivation grows from clear goals, small steps, tracking progress and rewarding success.

questions.question: The best summary of a healthy self-concept is…
options: knowing and valuing your real strengths and accepting growth areas
questions.expected: knowing and valuing your real strengths and accepting growth areas
questions.memo: A healthy self-concept is realistic: valuing strengths while accepting room to grow.

LO.G8.DS.A2.title: Sexuality
LO.G8.DS.A2.description: Development of the self in society (CAPS G8 T1) — Development of the self in society: Sexuality.
LO.G8.DS.A2.strand: Development of the self in society · Term 1
LO.G8.DS.A2.caps_topic: Development of the self in society
LO.G8.DS.A2.recovery_strategy: Sexuality is a natural part of who you are, shaped by your feelings, values and surroundings.

questions.question: In Life Orientation, 'sexuality' is best understood as…
options: a natural part of who you are as a person
questions.expected: a natural part of who you are as a person
questions.memo: Sexuality is a natural part of being human, linked to feelings, identity and values.

questions.question: Personal feelings can affect how a person understands their sexuality.
questions.memo: Personal feelings are part of understanding one's sexuality.

questions.question: Which can INFLUENCE a young person's view of their sexuality?
questions.memo: Friends, peers, family, culture and media all influence how someone understands sexuality.

questions.question: Working out who you are as a person is called identity ____.
questions.memo: Identity formation is the process of working out who you are, including your values.

questions.question: How can media create pressure around sexuality?
options: By showing unrealistic ideas as if they are normal
questions.expected: By showing unrealistic ideas as if they are normal
questions.memo: Media can present unrealistic or pressured ideas about sexuality and relationships.

questions.question: Family and community norms can shape attitudes toward sexuality.
questions.memo: Family and community norms are important influences on attitudes toward sexuality.

questions.question: A healthy attitude to questions about your own development is to…
options: seek accurate information from trusted adults
feel ashamed and ask no one
questions.expected: seek accurate information from trusted adults
questions.memo: Trusted adults and reliable sources give accurate information for healthy understanding.

questions.question: Respecting your own ____ and choices is part of healthy development.
questions.memo: Knowing and respecting your own values helps you make healthy choices.

questions.question: Peers can pressure each other about relationships and sexuality.
questions.memo: Peer influence and pressure can affect choices about relationships and sexuality.

questions.question: Why is it important to make your OWN informed choices about your body and relationships?
options: They affect your health, future and wellbeing
questions.expected: They affect your health, future and wellbeing
questions.memo: Informed personal choices protect your health, future and wellbeing.

questions.question: A friend feels confused about the changes and feelings of growing up. A caring response is to…
options: reassure them it is normal and suggest a trusted adult to talk to
tell them to keep it secret forever
questions.expected: reassure them it is normal and suggest a trusted adult to talk to
questions.memo: Reassurance and pointing to a trusted adult support a friend respectfully.
