questions.memo: Violence is linked to poverty, substance abuse, inequality and unresolved conflict.

questions.question: Solving disagreements without violence uses conflict-____ skills.
questions.memo: Conflict-management skills help resolve disagreements peacefully.

questions.question: Which is an ALTERNATIVE to violence?
questions.memo: Alternatives to violence include problem-solving and calm conflict management.

questions.question: Violence can harm both individual and community health and safety.
questions.memo: Violence damages the health and safety of individuals and whole communities.

questions.question: How can you protect yourself and others from violence?
options: Avoid risky situations and know where to get help
questions.expected: Avoid risky situations and know where to get help
questions.memo: Protection means avoiding risky situations and knowing where to find help.

questions.question: Reporting violence to the ____ can help keep people safe.
questions.memo: Reporting violence to the police or other authorities helps keep people safe.

questions.question: Responding to violence with more violence usually solves the problem.
questions.memo: Meeting violence with violence usually worsens it; peaceful solutions work better.

questions.question: Two learners are about to fight over an insult. A peaceful response is to…
options: calm down, talk it out or involve a teacher
questions.expected: calm down, talk it out or involve a teacher
questions.memo: Calming down, talking, or getting a teacher resolves conflict without violence.

questions.question: Which national programme aim helps reduce violence?
questions.memo: National health and safety promotion programmes help reduce violence and harm.

questions.question: Unmanaged anger can increase the risk of violence.
questions.memo: Anger that is not managed well can lead to violence; managing it reduces the risk.

questions.question: Where to find ____ includes the police, clinics and helplines.
questions.memo: Knowing where to find help — police, clinics, helplines — is key to staying safe.

questions.question: Why is it important to understand the impact of violence?
questions.memo: Understanding violence's harm motivates choosing peaceful alternatives.

questions.question: Schools can promote safety with clear rules and anti-bullying programmes.
questions.memo: Clear rules and anti-bullying programmes help schools promote safety.

questions.question: A good first response when you feel anger rising in a conflict is to…
options: pause, breathe, and step back before reacting
questions.expected: pause, breathe, and step back before reacting
questions.memo: Pausing and stepping back helps you respond calmly instead of violently.

questions.question: Sort each response to conflict into PEACEFUL or VIOLENT.
questions.expected: Talking calmly and mediation are peaceful; punching and threatening are violent.
questions.memo: Peaceful responses solve conflict; violent ones escalate it.

questions.question: Put the steps for managing a conflict without violence in order.

items.text: Look for a fair solution together
Get help if it cannot be resolved

questions.expected: Stay calm, listen to the problem, find a fair solution, then get help if needed.
questions.memo: Manage conflict by staying calm, listening, solving fairly and seeking help if needed.

questions.question: Knowing where to find help is an important part of staying safe.
questions.memo: Knowing where to find help — police, clinics, helplines — is key to safety.

questions.question: The key message about violence and safety is that…
options: conflict can be solved peacefully and help is available
questions.expected: conflict can be solved peacefully and help is available
questions.memo: Conflict can be managed peacefully, and help is always available.

LO.G9.CR.A1.title: Citizens' rights and national days
LO.G9.CR.A1.description: Constitutional rights & responsibilities (CAPS G9 T2) — Constitutional rights and responsibilities: Citizens' rights and national days.

questions.question: Respecting others' rights includes respecting people who are…

questions.memo: We must respect everyone's rights, including people living with disabilities and HIV and AIDS.

questions.question: What does Human Rights Day commemorate in South Africa?
options: The importance and protection of human rights

questions.question: Freedom Day celebrates South Africa's first democratic ____ in 1994.

questions.question: Why does South Africa celebrate national days?
options: To remember important events and shared values

questions.memo: National days mark important events and remind us of shared values.

questions.question: Heritage Day celebrates the diverse cultures of South Africa.
questions.memo: Heritage Day celebrates South Africa's diverse cultural heritage.

questions.question: Respecting the rights of people with disabilities means…
questions.memo: Respect means including people with disabilities and removing barriers to participation.

questions.question: Youth Day remembers the role of ____ in the struggle for freedom.

questions.question: Nelson Mandela Day encourages people to give time to help others.
questions.memo: Mandela Day encourages acts of service and helping others in the community.

questions.question: A learner uses a wheelchair and the class outing venue has stairs only. The rights-respecting response is to…
options: choose an accessible venue so everyone can join

questions.question: What is a responsibility that comes with the right to vote (as an adult)?
options: To make an informed, responsible choice

questions.question: Respecting others' rights helps create a fair and inclusive society.

questions.question: Reconciliation Day promotes national ____ and healing.

questions.question: Planning a local celebration of a national day helps citizens to…

questions.question: People living with HIV and AIDS have the same rights as everyone else.

questions.question: Which is a way to show responsible citizenship?
options: Respecting others' rights and obeying just laws
questions.expected: Respecting others' rights and obeying just laws
questions.memo: Responsible citizens respect rights and obey just laws.

questions.question: Sort each into RESPECTING rights or DISRESPECTING rights.

items.text: Including a learner with HIV normally

questions.expected: Accessibility and inclusion respect rights; exclusion and mockery disrespect them.
questions.memo: Respecting rights means including everyone; disrespect excludes or demeans.

questions.question: Put the steps for planning a local national-day celebration in order.

items.text: Choose the national day and its meaning
Hold the celebration with the community
Reflect on what was learned and shared

questions.expected: Choose the day and its meaning, plan inclusive activities, hold the event, then reflect.
questions.memo: Celebrate well by choosing the day's meaning, planning inclusively, holding it and reflecting.

questions.question: Women's Day honours the role of women in South Africa's history.
questions.memo: Women's Day commemorates the 1956 women's march and the role of women in our history.

questions.question: The key idea of citizens' rights and national days is that…
options: we respect everyone's rights and remember our shared history
questions.expected: we respect everyone's rights and remember our shared history
questions.memo: Responsible citizenship respects everyone's rights and honours our shared history.

LO.G9.CR.A2.title: Constitutional values

questions.question: Which is a value stated in the South African Constitution?

questions.question: Equality and human dignity are core constitutional values.

questions.question: What is a POSITIVE role model?
options: Someone whose good example is worth following
questions.expected: Someone whose good example is worth following
questions.memo: A positive role model sets a good example worth following.

questions.question: Treating everyone as equal upholds the value of ____.
questions.memo: Equality means treating everyone fairly and as equals, a core constitutional value.

questions.question: Who can be a role model for constitutional values?
questions.memo: Parents, teachers and community leaders can model constitutional values.

questions.question: Applying constitutional values in daily life means living them, not just knowing them.

questions.question: Which action shows the value of human dignity?
options: Treating others with respect and worth

questions.question: A NEGATIVE role model can lead others toward harmful choices.

questions.question: A leader treats all community members fairly regardless of background. This models…

questions.question: Why are constitutional values important for daily life?
options: They guide fair, respectful treatment of one another
questions.expected: They guide fair, respectful treatment of one another
questions.memo: Constitutional values guide how we treat one another fairly and respectfully.

questions.question: Freedom, as a constitutional value, comes with respecting others' freedom.
questions.memo: Freedom is balanced by the responsibility to respect others' freedom.

questions.question: Living constitutional values builds a fair and ____ society.

questions.question: Which is a good way for a learner to apply constitutional values?

questions.question: Non-sexism, treating all genders equally, is a constitutional value.

questions.question: A celebrity who cheats and brags about it is acting as a…

questions.question: Sort each action into UPHOLDS or VIOLATES constitutional values.
questions.expected: Equality and respect uphold values; racism and humiliation violate them.
questions.memo: Constitutional values are upheld by equality and dignity; violated by discrimination and cruelty.
